update_message: Pseudonyx 1.10.60 fixes four things reported from a real install. Attaching several documents at once to an AI website now works: they were all being checked and hidden correctly, and then not arriving at the website at all, because the two halves of the transfer disagreed about how long to wait and because some websites replace the file box while a batch is still going. The small message that appears on the page is readable again — its second line was blue text on a blue glow. You no longer get a Windows pop-up repeating a count the page has just shown you; it is said once, by whichever surface you were already looking at, and everything is still counted in your Insights. And in the first few minutes after installing, when the browser has not yet picked up the Pseudonyx extension, the message now tells you the one thing that ends the wait: close the browser and open it again. Nothing about detection or redaction changed, and nothing is unblocked earlier than before.
previous_update_message: Pseudonyx 1.5.86 can now tell you what it costs to run on your own computer. A new measurement writes down how much memory and how much time each setting actually uses, on your machine rather than ours, and the answers are published so you can choose settings knowing the trade instead of guessing. The short version: if your computer has 4 GB of memory, set redaction quality to Fast. Every check based on a pattern or a checksum still runs, so emails, phone numbers, bank accounts, cards, national numbers and IP addresses are all still caught. Your saved redactions also stop growing after five days, so the folder they live in settles at a size and stays there. Nothing about detection or redaction changed.

_note: download_url MUST start with licensing.downloadUrlAllowedPrefix in settings.json, currently
https://downloads.pseudonyx.org/releases/. The client REFUSES anything outside that prefix, so a URL
pointing anywhere else does not merely fail to download - it is dropped before any request is made and
no update can reach an installed user. Keys are immutable and versioned: never overwrite one.
latest_version TRACKS THE SOURCE BUILD and is asserted equal to the csproj <Version> by
VersionSingleSourceTests. An earlier note here said not to raise it until the R2 object exists, which
is a rule this repository breaks on every commit and a test enforces breaking - the two could not both
be obeyed, and the test won silently. HUMAN-ACTIONS 4b already documents the real consequence: on a
build that was copied rather than released, an update check offers a version it cannot fetch, and that
is expected rather than a bug.
WHAT ACTUALLY PROTECTS A USER IS THE ABSENCE OF THE OTHER TWO KEYS. installer_url and sha256 are what
UpdateDownloader needs, and a missing hash is refused exactly like a wrong one - so with them absent
nothing can auto-install and the app offers the download instead. Publish BOTH, together, only once the
signed object is in R2, and only with the POST-signing hash. Adding either one early is the only edit
here that can make a client execute a file.
download_url carries the version TWICE and must agree with latest_version; that is asserted by a test
now, because this URL has been hand-edited and left stale before - it sat at 1.10.22 while
latest_version said 1.10.24, so an install was told one version and handed another.

_what_this_is: Which browsers Pseudonyx SUPPORTS, meaning the browser where the live-typing extension, the native
bridge and the send-time verification have actually been exercised end to end. Chrome and Edge are
the two that have; every other browser is listed as unsupported and is therefore BLOCKED by default.
Blocking a browser is not the same thing as not protecting it. An unsupported browser is one where a
message could leave while the app still reported protection, and that is the single failure this
product exists to prevent. So the default answer is to close the browser rather than to watch it
with machinery nobody has verified there.
The user owns the final answer. Settings > Blocked browsers lists every browser here and the choice
is stored per browser in browsers.json, so a decision made by hand outlives any change to this file.
Supported: false + the user unticking it is a supported combination and it is honoured.
Names MUST match Live.BrowserCatalog exactly. A name that does not appear in the catalog can never
be identified on the wire, so it could never be enforced either; BrowserSupportListTests fails the
build rather than shipping an entry that silently does nothing.
File types Pseudonyx CANNOT redact, and therefore must NOT block. A video, a zip, an mp3 or an
installer has no text layer this product can rewrite, so refusing the upload buys the user nothing:
it only stops them working. Anything listed here is passed to the site exactly as they chose it.
IT LIVES IN companies.json ON PURPOSE. This is the file the application already re-syncs every day, so
a format we discover we cannot redact can be let through by a list update rather than by a release. It
used to be a standalone passthrough-extensions.json with a byte-identical copy inside the extension,
kept in step by a script and a drift test - two files, a tool and a test to say one thing.
THE BROWSER EXTENSION DOES NOT READ THIS FILE. It asks the application, which serves the list already
FILTERED through its own classifier. That matters because this file is remote-updatable: a bad list
push that added .pdf here could otherwise have sent documents to a model untouched. The application
drops any entry it recognises as redactable and logs it, so neither reader can be talked into a leak.
Re-read whenever this file changes, not once at startup. The extension re-pulls within one keep-alive
ping, because the ping already reports a stamp of these policy files and it already re-pulls on change.
_the_one_rule: ONLY put an extension here if we genuinely cannot redact it. This list is a hole in the protection by
design, so every entry must earn its place by being impossible rather than merely inconvenient.
In particular, DO NOT ADD:
- Images (.png .jpg .webp .gif .bmp .tiff .heic ...). Pseudonyx redacts these: it reads text out of
them with OCR and paints over it, and it detects and covers faces. They are among the most
valuable things it protects, not an exception to it.
- Documents (.pdf .docx .xlsx .pptx .odt .rtf .epub ...). All extracted and redacted.
- Anything text-shaped at all (.txt .csv .json .srt .vcf .sql, source code, config, notebooks).
See FileClassifier: unknown extensions that merely LOOK like text are redacted in place too, so
adding a text format here would create a leak in a format we handle perfectly well.
If you are unsure whether something is redactable, leave it out. Leaving it out means it is checked
and possibly refused, which is the safe direction; putting it in means it goes to the AI untouched.
AND NO AMBIGUOUS EXTENSIONS. Several extensions mean two unrelated things, and where one meaning is a
text format the entry has to go. Four were removed after being caught by a test rather than by eye:
.ts   MPEG transport stream, but overwhelmingly more often TypeScript source
.asm  a CATIA assembly, but also assembly-language source
.vhd  a Hyper-V disk image, but also VHDL source
.cue  a CD cue sheet, but also the CUE configuration language - and cue sheets are plain text anyway
The application would have survived all four, because FileClassifier checks its text tiers BEFORE this
list. So would the extension NOW, because the application filters the list before serving it. Neither
of those is a reason to leave a wrong entry here: a filtered-out entry is a line that reads as
protection-off and does nothing, and the next person to look will not know which of the two it is. A
test asserts the intersection with the redactable tiers is empty.
One extension, one dot. An entry like ".sav.spss" matches nothing at all - both readers key on the
final extension - so it is not a harmless extra, it is a line that looks like protection and is not.

video.why: No text layer we can rewrite. Redacting a moving image is a different product.

audio.why: Speech is not text until it is transcribed, and we do not transcribe. Nothing to rewrite.

why: A container's own bytes carry nothing to redact, and we do not unpack, redact and repack.
READ THIS BEFORE COPYING THE PATTERN. This group is the one real trade-off in this file: a zip of
CVs now reaches the AI unredacted where it used to be refused. That is a deliberate decision,
because refusing archives outright stopped people working and taught them to switch the product
off, which protects nothing at all. Deleting this group is a one-line change if you decide the
other way.
Note the packaged DOCUMENT formats that are technically zips - .docx .xlsx .pptx .odt .epub - are
NOT here. Those are recognised as documents and fully redacted.
Machine code. Nothing to redact, and rewriting a binary would corrupt it.
Note .obj is NOT here despite being a compiler's object file, because it is also the Wavefront 3D
format, which is plain text. Ambiguous wins go to the redactable meaning every time: a text .obj
now gets redacted, and a compiled one gets checked and possibly refused, which is the safe half.

disk_and_system_images.why: Whole filesystems. We cannot open, redact and rebuild one, and the file is usually enormous.

fonts.why: Glyph outlines and metrics tables. No user-authored content at all, and no text layer to rewrite.

why: We cannot read the contents, so we cannot redact them - and altering the bytes would break the
signature or the decryption. These are also, by definition, already protected.
Opaque binary containers. Text SQL dumps (.sql, .ddl) are NOT here - those are redacted in place.
This is only the compiled/binary forms we cannot rewrite safely.

machine_learning_models.why: Weights. Enormous, opaque, and nothing a person wrote.

why: Proprietary BINARY geometry. Note .svg is NOT here: it is XML and is redacted in place.
The interchange formats that are TEXT by specification were removed for the same reason as .svg -
.step .stp .iges .igs (ASCII), .gltf (JSON), .dae (XML), .usda (text) and .eps (PostScript). The
application's LooksLikeText sniff redacts an unknown text file in place, so listing a text format
here would punch a hole in a format we already handle correctly. .stl and .ply stay because both
have a binary form that is what tools actually export, and .abc/.usdc/.glb are binary siblings.
Instrument and capture formats with no rewritable text layer. RAW photographs are here because we
cannot re-encode a camera raw without destroying it - unlike ordinary images, which ARE redacted.
The ASCII members were removed for the same reason as the CAD ones: .gcode, .hex, .s19 and .srec
are plain text, so the application redacts them in place and they must not be waved through.

_data_note: FOUR COMPANIES, SEVENTEEN WEBSITES, TWELVE REDACTED HOSTS (three were removed on 30 August 2026, below). This list was cut from 349 companies / 457 hosts to exactly
the four vendors and the websites named in docs/AI_Companies_Matrix.md. The matrix names twenty addresses,
but several are PATHS on one host (chatgpt.com/canvas, /sites, /voice; claude.ai/artifacts, /@projects), and
policy here is enforced per HOST - a path cannot be matched by the PAC, the proxy or a match pattern. So the
twenty collapse to the fifteen hosts below with no loss of coverage. Everything the product does is driven from
here: the PAC intercept set, the upload proxy, the blocking page, the extension's static match patterns
(generated - run tools/sync-extension-manifest.ps1) and the native-app gates. Adding a host here is a
protection decision, not a cosmetic one.
`verified` IS PER COMPANY, NOT PER HOST, and that used to matter for five of these addresses. THREE OF
THE FIVE ARE NOW GONE. `verified` means the site's own composer, send gesture and upload path have
actually been exercised, and it is what admits a host to the extension's static injection set. These
have been exercised: chatgpt.com, gemini.google.com, aistudio.google.com, notebooklm.google.com,
labs.google, copilot.microsoft.com, bing.com, claude.ai, console.anthropic.com, huggingface.co.
REMOVED FROM THE REDACTED TIER on 30 August 2026 (HUMAN-ACTIONS W8.14, AI-TODO A22):
azure.microsoft.com, designer.microsoft.com and deepmind.google. All three were documentation or
marketing surfaces with no chat composer, so the injected script stood down on every one of them: they
cost an access permission and bought nothing, while `verified` claimed coverage nothing had exercised.
designer.microsoft.com went too even though it is an image tool where uploads happen with nothing to
type into - a partial exception would have re-created exactly the claim the removal exists to retire.
The three are NOT added to the blocked tier. Blocking would close a Microsoft documentation site and a
research page some users legitimately want open, a cost the decision did not ask for. They are simply
unlisted now, which is what every other site on the internet is.
Microsoft AI KEEPS `Microsoft Designer` in `titles`, deliberately. `titles` is the window-title fallback
for NATIVE apps (SitePolicyStore.ProtectedNativeApp) - a different channel from hosts, and W8.14 decided
the host tier. Removing it would have changed native-app behaviour nothing decided.
TWO of the five remain unexercised and inherit the company flag without evidence of their own:
platform.openai.com and copilot.cloud.microsoft. Both have real composers, so they need a live pass
rather than a decision - AI-TODO A17.
notebook.google.com ADDED 31 August 2026, AND A VENDOR RENAME HAD LEFT IT COMPLETELY UNPROTECTED FOR SIX
WEEKS. Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on 16 July 2026 and moved it to notebook.google.com.
That host was in NO tier - not redacted, not blocked - so the content script was never injected and typing
there was watched by nothing. Reported by a user typing two names into it and seeing neither redacted.
notebooklm.google.com is KEPT alongside it: an old bookmark or a redirect must not lose protection, and
removing a host is the one edit here that can only ever remove cover.
It is ALSO unexercised and inherits `verified` from the company, so it belongs on A17's list with the two
above. That is the safe direction and it is not a free pass: protection running on an unexercised host is
better than no protection, and the claim is tracked rather than assumed.
THE RENAME WAS HALF-SEEN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING. The blocked-tier Google Gemini entry had
already gained `Gemini Notebook` in its `titles` - so somebody noticed the new NAME and updated the
native-app matcher, while the new HOST was never added anywhere. Titles and hosts are different channels
and a rename touches both; updating one reads as having handled it. See AI-TODO A32.
Recording it here rather than silently, because the rule this project already fixed once was exactly this:
decorating a site we cannot protect is worse than leaving it alone, since a highlight reads as a promise.
TWO TIERS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS NOT OPTIONAL. The four entries below are REDACTED: verified, redact:true,
and the only ones the browser extension is ever told to watch. Everything after them is BLOCKED: redact is
false and verified is absent, so BuildHostCompanyMap excludes them and no content script is injected, but
blocked:true puts their hosts into BlockedHosts() and from there into a declarativeNetRequest rule and the
proxy PAC blackhole tier, so the site does not open at all.
The blocked tier was briefly DELETED when the list was consolidated onto four vendors, and that was a
fail-open regression rather than a simplification: removing an entry does not just stop us redacting a
service, it stops us RECOGNISING it, so ~345 AI sites the product had always refused to open began loading
normally with no protection of any kind. Blocking what we cannot redact is the fail-closed answer.
NO BLOCKED HOST MAY EQUAL, CONTAIN OR SIT UNDER A REDACTED ONE. Block rules match a domain AND its
subdomains, so a blocked parent would blackhole a redacted child - blocking anthropic.com would have closed
console.anthropic.com. Eight hosts were dropped for that reason when this tier was rebuilt:
gemini.google.com, aistudio.google.com, notebooklm.google.com, labs.google, copilot.microsoft.com,
bing.com and huggingface.co now belong to a redacting vendor, and edgeservices.bing.com is a subdomain of
the redacted bing.com. Microsoft Bing lost its only host that way and is gone. A test asserts the two
tiers never intersect in any of those three directions.
PROMPT APPLICATIONS ONLY. Microsoft AI's apps.processes lists Copilot and nothing else. It used to list
WINWORD, EXCEL, POWERPNT and OUTLOOK too, because those host a Copilot pane and pasting into that pane was
therefore covered. The cost was not worth it: an email client is not a prompt application, and treating it
as one put a redaction preview over an email the user had merely RECEIVED (1.10.0). Word, Excel,
PowerPoint and Outlook are now out of the redacting set entirely - no paste protection, no overlay, no
send gate - on the owner's instruction that only AI prompt applications are redacted.
THE FOUR STAY IN send_gate_exempt_processes, and that list now means NEVER AN AI DESTINATION rather than
merely 'do not hold Enter here'. Removing them from apps.processes alone was not enough: a native app that
matches no process still falls back to WINDOW TITLE matching, and this company's titles include the whole
word 'Copilot' - so an email whose subject mentioned Copilot would have been read as an AI destination and
the overlay would have returned on exactly the surface this change exists to clear. The JSON key keeps its
name for schema stability; the C# accessor is SitePolicyStore.NeverAnAiDestination, which says what it does.
